blocking_dependencies: OSSL_provider_init -> phase 13 (providers/legacy/legacyprov.c's entry point, and the name a third-party provider's own entry point is declared with -- which is why subphase rows 6.8d and 6.12 name it, since the `providers` configuration module needs a module path and RT-PROVIDER-3P compiles its own. The authority symbol is the legacy provider's, so it is Phase 13's.)

evp_app_cleanup_int -> phase 8 (Defined in `crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c` and called from `crypto/evp/names.c`'s `EVP_cleanup_int`, so two transcribed units now owe it. Its whole body is `sk_EVP_PKEY_METHOD_pop_free(app_pkey_methods, EVP_PKEY_meth_free)`: both the stack and the destructor belong to the **application-supplied `EVP_PKEY_METHOD` registry**, which is 7.4l's because `EVP_PKEY_meth_find`'s lookup searches `standard_methods[]` -- the table whose contents are Phase 8's objects under D163 and D165. So this is Phase 8's with its sibling rows rather than a same-subphase deferral: there is no 7.4c-ii or 7.4d that could land it, because the two symbols it needs do not exist until Phase 8 does.)

evp_cleanup_int -> phase 7 (Internal, called only by `OPENSSL_cleanup`, and **owed to 7.4 inside this stratum**. Its body is seven calls: four `OBJ_NAME_cleanup`, then `EVP_PBE_cleanup` -- which is `crypto/evp/evp_pbe.c`'s, a 7.4 unit that does not exist yet -- then `OBJ_sigid_free`, then `evp_app_cleanup_int`. So half of it cannot be written, and the half that could would have to omit the other half. `owner_phase` is 7 rather than a later stratum because the dependency is a later *subphase* of the same stratum, which is why it appears in the blocking census rather than in a hand-off edge.)

evp_pkey_copy_downgraded -> phase 8 (The fourth of the seven and the one that makes the other three wait. Its body exports the provider keydata through `evp_keymgmt_export` -- this stratum's -- and then imports it with `(*dest)->ameth->import_from`, synchronising `(*dest)->ameth->dirty_cnt`. Two fields of an `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` and one of that struct's function pointers are read directly, so the function cannot be written before an ameth object exists, and the ameth objects are the twelve `crypto/asn1/ameth_lib.c` builds from Phase 8's `standard_methods[]`. It also needs `EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey`, which is `pmeth_lib.c`'s and lands in 7.4c *inside* this stratum -- so the order is 7.4c, then Phase 8, then this row.)

evp_pkey_ctx_get_params_strict -> phase 7 (Internal to `crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c`, declared in `include/crypto/evp.h`, so the gate owes it now that 7.4c-i has given that unit a module. Its body is a three-line guard over `evp_keymgmt_get_params` -- it refuses unless the context is an `EVP_PKEY_OP_FROMDATA` operation with a live algorithm context -- and it is owed to the **second half of this same subphase** (`owner_phase` 7, the `evp_cleanup_int` precedent) because 7.4c-ii is where the params path lands beside it. Its callers are `pmeth_gn.c` and `m_sigver.c`, both 7.4's.)

evp_pkey_ctx_set_params_strict -> phase 7 (The setter half of the same pair, and it has the same three-line shape with `evp_keymgmt_set_params` in place of the getter. Recorded separately because the gate owes *names* rather than call graphs: a reader of the blocking census should see both rather than one and an implication.)

evp_pkey_ctx_use_cached_data -> phase 7 (Internal to `crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c`, and the *replay* half of the cached-data trio whose store and free halves 7.4c-i landed. Its body tests `dist_id_set` and then hands the distinguishing identifier to `evp_pkey_ctx_ctrl_str_int` or `evp_pkey_ctx_ctrl_int` -- the ctrl machinery, which is 7.4c-ii's. So it is owed to the second half of this same subphase, and its three callers (`signature.c`, `exchange.c`, `pmeth_gn.c`) are the operation inits that land with the ctrl path beside it.)

evp_pkey_decrypt_alloc -> phase 7 (Internal to `crypto/evp/asymcipher.c` and declared in `include/crypto/evp.h`, so the gate owes it the moment the crate has a module for that unit -- which 7.4b-i's method half gave it. Its body is the two-pass auto-allocating decrypt: call `EVP_PKEY_decrypt(ctx, NULL, outlenp, in, inlen)` to learn the length, `OPENSSL_malloc` it, call again, then refuse if the second call failed, the length came back zero, or a non-zero `expected_outlen` disagrees. So it is owed to the **operation half of the same subphase** (`owner_phase` 7, the `evp_cleanup_int` precedent) because `EVP_PKEY_decrypt` is `asymcipher.c`'s own and lands directly beside it. Its two callers are `crypto/pkcs7/pk7_doit.c` and `crypto/cms/cms_env.c`, both Phase 12's, which is why nothing reaches it yet.)

evp_pkey_free_legacy -> phase 8 (One of the seven functions `include/crypto/evp.h` declares for `crypto/evp/p_lib.c`, and so one the gate owes the moment the crate has a module for that unit (D163, the `a2d_ASN1_OBJECT` class in the other direction). Its body needs `x->ameth`, an `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD *`, and the branch that finds one when the key has only a legacy cache entry calls `EVP_PKEY_asn1_find` -- the registry `crypto/asn1/ameth_lib.c` builds from `standard_methods[]`, whose twelve objects are the algorithm strata's and are Phase 8's contents. There is also an `ameth->pkey_free` call through the found method, so the free path is not merely gated on the table's existence: it *is* the table.)

evp_pkey_get0_DH_int -> phase 8 (The third of the seven, and the shortest: it is `pkey->type == EVP_PKEY_DH ? evp_pkey_get_legacy(pkey) : NULL`. It is therefore blocked by nothing of its own and inherited entirely from its sibling above -- the DH *type* it compares against is real now, the downgrade it calls is not. Recorded separately rather than folded into `evp_pkey_get_legacy` because the gate owes names, not call graphs, and a reader of the blocking census should see all four rather than three and an implication.)

evp_pkey_get_legacy -> phase 8 (The second of the seven. It downgrades a provider key to a legacy one, so its whole body past the fast paths is `evp_pkey_copy_downgraded`, and the cache it then holds is keyed on `ameth` being non-NULL (`EVP_PKEY_asn1_find` for the type). Both halves are Phase 8's, which is why this name waits on the same registry as its sibling rather than on anything in this stratum.)

evp_rand_can_seed -> phase 9 (Internal: declared in `include/crypto/evp.h`, which is not installed, and its only caller in the whole authority is `crypto/rand/rand_lib.c`, already recorded in this file's `units` section as Phase 9's. 7.3f transcribes `evp_rand.c` and deliberately stops at the dispatch walk that fills the `get_seed` and `clear_seed` *fields*: the fields are this file's, the three callers are the stratum that needs the DRBG plumbing. Recording the name here is what makes that boundary visible to the gate rather than only to a reader.)

evp_rand_clear_seed -> phase 9 (The third of the seed trio, and the same boundary again: internal, declared in the uninstalled `include/crypto/evp.h`, called only by `crypto/rand/rand_lib.c`, and the releasing half of the pair whose acquiring half is `evp_rand_get_seed`. Neither half has a caller before Phase 9.)

evp_rand_get_seed -> phase 9 (The same boundary as its `can_seed` sibling: internal to `crypto/evp/evp_rand.c`, declared in the uninstalled `include/crypto/evp.h`, called only by `crypto/rand/rand_lib.c`. It answers entropy to the DRBG, so it cannot be written before the thing that asks for entropy exists.)
ossl_get_enginesdir -> phase 16 (The OPENSSL_info strings rather than anything the registry reads)
ossl_get_openssldir -> phase 16 (The OPENSSL_info strings rather than anything the registry reads; so is its sibling)
ossl_get_wininstallcontext -> phase 16 (A Windows-only string the admitted Linux/x86-64 profile does not build, carried with its two siblings rather than special-cased)

ossl_random_add_conf_module -> phase 9 (One of the seven modules `OPENSSL_load_builtin_modules` registers. It is Phase 9's because it lives in crypto/rand/rand_lib.c, and the fan-out's residual -- six of the seven absent -- is already recorded in the Phase 6 subphase plan and the seal; this row is what makes the name visible to the gate rather than only to a reader.)
body.census_not_a_failure: the C language surface is counted and listed, never failed: the crate models C types, macros and reason codes differently on purpose, and a lexical scan cannot tell a rename from a gap
body.claim: A structural gate, not a parity claim. It answers whether a dependency has an owner and whether the owner arrives in time; it says nothing about whether the dependency behaves as the authority's does.
body.rule: every authority-internal name a crate module references must be built by the crate or recorded with the stratum that owns it; every internal function a transcribed authority unit calls must exist, unless a divergence record covering exactly that name says why not; and a divergence record may not cover a name the gate did not observe

sealed_stratum_census.definition: authority internal functions a transcribed unit calls, whose own translation unit's stratum has already sealed. Not a failure: each is either modelled differently by the crate or is work carried across the boundary by a later stratum. The count is held to non-increase by the regression guard.
